title: fix: keep unrelated state handlers out of streamed reads
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160765
Follow-up to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176082

## What Problem This Solves

State-read workers load unrelated handlers when restoring subagent records or exporting transcripts. The deployed bundle also pulls the mixed read/write registry owner into the export dependency graph.

## User Impact

These reads load only their selected stream owner. Admission, snapshot, backpressure, cancellation, and cleanup behavior are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

This does not establish 1GiB or 512MiB Gateway support or quantify a memory reduction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the selected lazy stream before fresh admission, then execute it within the existing native section. Move restore into a dedicated reader and preserve the owner boundaries in the deployed bundle.

The main integration preserves the newer PostgreSQL bridge and workspace-manifest dispatch, and keeps restore transaction-free. Its existing no-explicit-transaction regression now targets the extracted reader.

## Evidence

Focused validation of the integrated candidate on Node 24.22.1:
- All 16 worker tests passed, including publication, bridge-prestart, and stream admission cases.
- All 3 artifact tests passed: native assets and both standalone/deployed import closures. Fresh children also exercised canonical restore and transcript export through the emitted worker, verified results, and joined cleanup.
- All 4 selected SQLite regressions passed: no explicit transaction, bounded snapshot streaming, cancellation without partial publication, and quarantine refusal.
- Scoped formatting, both typed-lint selections, and all four selected type graphs passed.
- All 19 eager import-closure regressions passed after adding the stream helper to the native PR-wrapper inventory. This repairs the three failures in the previous head's CI run.
- Independent source review passed. Formal branch review of all eleven changed paths at `4ea091b661092c399104b8e61e0c1ed7d6f8fc3d` found no actionable P0 defects; lower priorities were outside that formal threshold.

Historical limitation: an earlier local changed-check run on the previous source exceeded the 720-root boundary in Gateway/plugin graphs (723/724); its import-closure check was not reached. The broad boundary check has not been rerun against this corrected candidate; the historical result is not attributed to it. The focused import-closure suite has now passed. Required CI on the updated exact head is not yet qualified and remains independently enforced.
